content.user_title: Manage tzst Archives from the CLI
content.value_statement: Archive workflows can fail when flags, filters, or conflict rules are unclear. This skill gives focused tzst CLI guidance for safe extraction, automation, and installation.
actual_capabilities: Choose tzst subcommands for creating, extracting, listing, and testing archives.
Recommend safe extraction filters, including data, tar, and fully_trusted modes.
Prepare JSON-friendly command patterns for scripts and pipelines.
Explain conflict-resolution choices for interactive and automated extraction.
Guide installation through uv, pip, or official release binaries.
Troubleshoot exit codes and command placement for global flags.
limitations: It covers the tzst CLI, not the Python API or generic tar and zip tools.
It cannot verify archive contents without access to the files.
It does not replace user review before installing packages or binaries.
It relies on the installed tzst version for final flag behavior.

use_cases.title: Safe Backup Extraction
use_cases.description: Choose extraction commands, filters, and conflict rules for restoring archives without flattening paths by mistake.

use_cases.title: Scriptable Archive Checks
use_cases.description: Prepare machine-readable list or test workflows with stable exit-code handling and non-interactive conflict choices.

use_cases.title: tzst Install Support
use_cases.description: Guide users through uv, pip, or release binary setup before running version and help checks.

prompt_templates.title: Check a tzst Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: List the contents of backup.tzst and explain whether I should use normal or flat extraction.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract backup.tzst into restore/ using safe defaults and preserve the original directory structure.

prompt_templates.title: Automate JSON Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a non-interactive command to list backup.tzst as JSON without banner text for a pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Trusted Extraction Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare data, tar, and fully_trusted filters for this archive source, then recommend the safest command and conflict policy.

output_examples.input: I need to extract a backup but keep folders intact.
output_examples.output: Use normal extraction, keep the data filter, and choose an output folder. Avoid flat extraction unless you need one directory.

output_examples.input: I need archive output for automation.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends machine-readable output, no banner text, and a non-interactive conflict strategy before running the command.

output_examples.input: This archive came from an unknown source.
output_examples.output: The skill keeps the data filter, avoids fully trusted mode, and suggests listing contents before extracting selected members.

best_practices: List an archive first when member names or structure are uncertain.
Use the data extraction filter unless the archive source is fully trusted.
Set a non-interactive conflict policy for scripts and scheduled jobs.
anti_patterns: Using flat extraction when the user expects directory structure to remain.
Combining machine-readable output with interactive conflict prompts.
Recommending fully trusted extraction for unknown archive sources.

faq.question: Does this skill install tzst automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest uv, pip, or release binaries when the user asks for installation help.

faq.question: Can it work with tar or zip archives?
faq.answer: Only when tzst is part of the task. Generic tar or zip questions are outside its scope.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the safest extraction filter?
faq.answer: Use the data filter for normal and untrusted archives. Use fully trusted mode only for fully trusted sources.

faq.question: Can it produce automation-friendly commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend machine-readable output and explicit conflict rules for scripts.

faq.question: Can it inspect my archive contents by itself?
faq.answer: No. It needs the agent or user to run tzst against available files.
